passage:
Students often charged phones in classroom outlets. Cords crossed walkways, and one student tripped.
The school made a charging station near the office. Students could charge devices there during lunch, but not in classrooms.
Some students complained because it was less convenient. The school explained that safety came first.
The student council added numbered spaces so phones would not be mixed up.
The rule solved more than one problem: fewer cords, less distraction, and safer rooms.
Modern schools must manage modern objects. Electricity may be everywhere, but using it carelessly can turn convenience into danger.
